title: Cost Governance — Signal Taxonomy, Initiative Calendar, and Cycle Playbook
creator: Marina Chen
description:
Purpose: Establish an operational 'Cost Governance' layer that ties measurable cost signals (batch hit rate, KV cache hit, quantization regression risk, per-token latency) to a recurring initiative calendar and a cycle-level playbook. Goal: make cost-reduction experiments (batching, caching, quantization) predictable, measurable, and safe to roll out across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Why this is needed: We run many parallel econ experiments with divergent metrics and inconsistent rollout criteria. This causes noisy signal, accidental regressions, and missed savings. A single taxonomy and calendar will improve experiment hygiene, reduce customer risk, and accelerate measurable savings.

Scope:
- Define a signal taxonomy and guardrails for cost experiments.
- Create a 6-cycle initiative calendar (quarterly cadence) that sequences experiments across product, eng, and design.
- Produce a cycle playbook with gating criteria, rollback triggers, and evaluation templates.
- Integrate with Console dashboards and the Optimize recommendation engine for automated alerts and guardrail enforcement.

Out of scope: full automation of rollouts (that remains infra/ENG work). This ticket is PM-level orchestration + artifacts and owners.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Signal taxonomy doc approved by Eng/Research/Console teams.
2) Initiative calendar published with owners for next 6 cycles.
3) Cycle playbook template (PRD + eval checklist) uploaded to Confluence and linked in Console runbook.
4) Three pilot experiments (one batching, one cache-prefetch, one quantization-profile) scheduled in next cycle with clear metrics and rollback thresholds.
5) Stakeholder review recorded (notes + approvals).

updates:
2026-02-10 — Marina Chen created ticket and invited stakeholders (ENG infra, Research, Console, Design). Initial hypotheses: 12-18% achievable token-cost reduction across low-latency workloads without SLO violations if batching and KV prefetch are coordinated.

2026-02-24 — Working group kickoff; attendees: Daniel Kim (PM lead), Priya Ramesh (Infra), Jorge Alvarez (Research), Hana Lee (Console), Lucas Grant (Design). Agreed to use three canonical workload archetypes: Conversational low-latency, Single-shot summarization, Large-context embeddings.

2026-03-02 — Draft taxonomy circulated. Key signals proposed: avg tokens/session, batching efficiency (avg batch size, tail batch latency), KV cache hit rate (prefix and dynamic), quantization delta (ppl/regression proxies), retry & fallback ratio, per-route cost-per-token. Requested ENG instrumentation tasks (ENG-22411) to add per-route quantization metrics.

2026-03-10 — Cross-functional review held. Feedback: Research requests standard eval harness (PR: github.com/redwood-research/econ-harness/pull/78) and baseline repro to be linked. Console asks for a new dashboard tile for 'Cost Signal Health'. Action: finalize taxonomy by 2026-03-18 and produce playbook template.
risks:
- Measurement divergence: different teams may compute signals differently (mitigation: canonical metrics definitions and example SQL queries).
- Regressions in quality when applying aggressive quantization (mitigation: rollout gates + human-in-loop checks + eval set).
- Overlap with existing cost initiatives (mitigation: align with PM-50121 and ENG owners).
- Console dashboard slippage could delay automated guardrails (mitigation: schedule manual gating until dashboard is ready).
decisions:
- Use three workload archetypes for taxonomy (agreed 2026-02-24).
- Require both absolute and relative guardrail thresholds per experiment (e.g., <0.5% delta in task-level accuracy OR explicit rollback).
- All quantization experiments must include reproducible quality evals and a staging rollout to Dedicated before Hosted.
